transcript.text: AEG IKB64301FB induction hob keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off. Pan of pasta boiled over just before.

The 'ER03' code on AEG hobs often relates to a safety fault detected by the control system. Given that your pasta boiled over immediately before this happened, it is highly likely that liquid has tracked underneath the glass surface or into the control area, triggering a short-circuit protection or earth-leakage detection. Please switch the hob off at the wall (isolate it) and leave it completely dry for 24 hours. Do not use it during this time. After 24 hours, try switching it back on without any pans to see if the error clears. If the error persists or returns quickly after drying, there may be permanent damage to the control PCB from the spillage, which would require a qualified engineer to inspect.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
I've already wiped it dry and switched it off at the wall for 5 minutes, and it works again now, all four zones fine. Do I still need to leave it 24 hours?
You can use your hob again, but please be careful to wipe up any spills immediately in future to prevent liquid from tracking underneath the controls.

candidates: Spillage tracking causing a safety fault or short circuit (high)
Control PCB failure due to moisture ingress (medium)

reading.symptom: keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make AEG; model IKB64301FB; code ER03.
The fault they reported is: "keeps beeping and showing Er03 then switches off". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

claimsRejected.claim: it reset after a short power cycle

reading.symptom: error code after pasta boiled over

plan: They asked: "Do I still need to leave it 24 hours?" - answer that first.
The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.

facts.value: wiped dry and switched off at the wall for 5 minutes: works again now, all four zones fine
